moves.why: Central socket 8 has four neighbors and gives me flexibility to extend a same-species grove in any direction; bracket is common so the placement doesn't telegraph where my scarce stools will go

Pass — probing my own plant wastes a pin and broadcasts free information (it confirms bracket to seat 1); crowning now commits a crown to a single bracket (1 point if uncontested) when I'd rather save crowns for a paired grove worth 4 points or a hollow/inkcap that's worth 2 per single when doubled
planting at a far corner keeps options open and sets up an adjacent pair for my second bracket later, while seat 0's center plant doesn't pressure this region
probing seat 0's upper reveals bracket vs deadhead (bracket matches, so still 1/3) but mostly costs seat 0 info; my own bracket is public knowledge to me, no need to probe

Plant bracket next to mine at 9 to start a same-species pair — that gives a potential 4-point uncontested grove; seat 1 probed my 8's upper (sunk = bracket confirmed), so seat 1 knows exactly one bracket sits at 8 and is likely contesting or building around it

Probe seat 1's socket 0 lower — I need to learn whether seat 1's 0 is scarce (sunk = inkcap/hollow) since seat 1 planted there right after my bracket; if it's deadhead/bracket the common pair is uninteresting, but a sunk pin tells me seat 1 is building a double-scoring scarce grove I must contest or crown before they consolidate
plant my second bracket at position 1, adjacent to my first at position 0, locking in a 2-stool bracket grove before seat 0 can build one; seat 0 has revealed bracket at 8 so they may also pair there

probing my own bracket at 0 lower tells me if it pairs with another bracket (sunk means another bracket=2-grove) but I already know it's bracket; probing seat 0's 9 lower would reveal their second stool — and if it's bracket they can pair with 8 to build a 2-grove I can't match. But that's also info I could use later. Actually probing my own is wasteful. Probing seat 0's 9 upper: if proud→deadhead, if sunk→bracket. Best to deny seat 0 the safety of that info while I learn it — probe 9 upper.

Plant inkcap at socket 7 — neighbors include seat 1's socket 1 and my own 8, maximizing the chance of forming a contested 2-stool inkcap grove (worth 4 each when doubled) if seat 1 plays their inkcap or hollow adjacent; even if no pair forms, a 1-stool inkcap grove with my crown scores 2 points

Probe my own inkcap at 7 lower to confirm it's not a hollow (both sunk = hollow) — I want to know if I have the rarer of the scarce pair sitting there before deciding whether to crown it for the double score, since inkcap and hollow both double but hollow is the more contestable target
planting hollow at 17 (far corner, far from seat 0's known bracket at 8-9) — hollow is scarce and double-scoring; putting it isolated keeps it out of any contested grove with seat 0

probing seat 0's bracket at 8 lower would split deadhead vs bracket — if proud it's deadhead, if sunk bracket. But seat 0 has shown they plant carefully and pair things; I want info on 7 (inkcap likely) and 9 (their second stool). Probing 7 upper tells me inkcap vs deadhead; inkcap is the only scarce I should worry about contesting. But wasting a probe on my own hollow is silly — pass and save pin for later.

Plant hollow at 16 — it's adjacent to seat 1's hollow at 17, so I can pair our hollows into a contested 2-stool grove (worth 4 each doubled) or seat 1 will avoid it and I can crown a singleton for 2 doubled
Crown my hollow at 16 — paired with seat 1's hollow at 17 it's a contested double-scoring grove worth 4 points (n=2, doubled) and now I've staked the claim before seat 1 can unbalance it

plant my inkcap (scarce, double-scoring) at position 2 — adjacent to my bracket pair at 0-1. If seat 0 can't reach it, the inkcap sits alone but still scores 1×2=2 double. Better than deadhead which scores nothing solo.

crown my own inkcap at 2 — even if it's a lone grove it scores 1×1×2=2 double, but if I can grow it into a 2-grove (next to my bracket at 1, but inkcap doesn't connect to bracket by species) — inkcap is its own species so it stays a grove of 1 unless I plant another inkcap adjacent. Best use: crown it to claim it; I have 3 crowns and 3 planted, this locks value.

Plant deadhead at 4 — central-ish, far from contested zones so seat 1's last probe can't threaten it; deadhead is my only species that can't form a valuable grove so placement is low-stakes, just consume the turn

Crown seat 1's hollow at 17 — it pairs with my hollow at 16 to form a contested 2-stool hollow grove (doubles to worth 4 each, so I'd score 4 if uncontested-but-contested is 2; wait, contested gives n=2, doubled = 4; if I don't crown, the grove is ignored entirely); a single crown from me is enough since seat 1 already has nothing on it

plant deadhead at 3, extending my row adjacent to my inkcap at 2 — deadhead is junk but it costs nothing to plant. If seat 0 ever reveals inkcap next to mine I'd lose the uncontested claim, but planting elsewhere doesn't help. Choose 3 to keep a contiguous block.
crown my bracket at 1 (or 0) — but I only have 1 crown left. Bracket pair at 0-1 is grove of 2; uncontested for me = 2×2=4. That's my biggest swing. Crown 1.
Plant deadhead at 4 — last stool, just need to plant somewhere; 4 is interior, doesn't extend any opponent's potential groves, and doesn't matter much since deadhead is worth nothing

Crown my inkcap at 7 — it's a singleton scarce grove, doubled = 2 points; that's my last crown so I should place it on something real, and my bracket pair at 8-9 already has no crown and won't beat seat 1's lead

plant my last deadhead anywhere — pick 15 (far corner, far from contested center) to fill my last required plant. Where doesn't matter for scoring (deadhead alone = 0); seat 0 is ahead and I need to just complete.

I have one crown left and need to maximize. Bracket pair 0-1 uncontested = 2×2=4. If seat 0 has any bracket adjacent to either 0 or 1, the grove grows and I lose the uncontested bonus. I have no pins left info-wise. Crown 1 to lock it.
Pass — closing round, all my crowns placed, no more planting; probing anything just gives seat 1 free information in a game I'm already losing and won't change my score
closing round, no crowns left to place, probing only helps if I could crown after (can't) — no further scoring moves available. Pass.
